AI & Settings

How the model thinks, how much data it has learned from, and every system parameter

Two AI layers in the app

1 · XGBoost — price prediction (trained in-app)

Trains itself on Binance candles per pair × timeframe: outputs Prob (probability of price going UP), bias LONG/SHORT, ATR-based SL/TP. Each retrain improves it (or is rejected if it regressed). This is the model that DECIDES to open trades.

2 · Qwen 7B (llama-server) — risk supervisor

A local language model reads the pending trade context (prob, R:R, timeframe, whale) and only VETOES or APPROVES — no price prediction, no retraining. It is the final 'risk officer' checkpoint.

❓ Is llama-server (Qwen2.5-7B) used for finetuning?

NO. llama-server only runs inference for risk review. 'Finetune' in this app means XGBoost retraining itself on fresh candles + lessons from closed dry-run trades (champion–challenger: 4 hyper candidates compete, winner kept). Qwen never gets its weights tuned.

What is Prob — and how to read it?

Raw prob = probability of price going UP (P up) from XGBoost on the validation split, Platt-calibrated for reliability against realized outcomes. Prob is displayed ALONG THE LEANED SIDE: SHORT Prob 79.9% means 79.9% confidence price goes DOWN (not 20.1% up).

Do not read prob as true win probability. Compare the reliability table RIGHT BELOW (computed on closed dry-run trades + scored PHE suggestions — not the val split): whatever win rate the 80%+ bucket really achieves is the honest expectation. High prob means the model is DECISIVE, not RIGHT.

Prob reliability — measured on REAL data

Displayed prob vs realized win rate — not val-split accuracy (val is only ~100 pure-candle rows, so the Platt curve itself is noisy and optimistic).

How much data has the AI learned?

Every train/finetune run is persisted. samples = training rows (candles + lessons), val = out-of-sample check rows (pure candles, no lessons).

No persisted run in THIS server's DB yet — press Train on the dashboard. Note: train history is per DEPLOYMENT (localhost and elliott.huyenbao.com have separate DBs; git syncs code only).

Trade autopsy — why wins, why losses

Every CLOSED paper trade (win AND loss) is dissected by the LLM on real candle paths (MFE/MAE/noise/R). Lessons are fed back into future reviews of the same pair — a closed learning loop.

No autopsies yet — they appear after the first paper trade closes (LLM timeout 300s each, runs in background).

Strategy self-evolution

The lab builds candidates from integrated data (feature importance + grid) and the LLM adds one more → backtests them on real candles with the engine's own algorithm → applies the winner → watches real paper trades → auto-reverts if worse than baseline.

No evolution round yet — the first one runs 10 minutes after deploy.

Root-cause analysis

Sends the full /stats snapshot to the Risk Officer. Output is English-only: consistency, ranked risks, verdict, and up to 3 concrete parameter actions (gates, stake, TF).

Open the stats page → /statsEnglish RCA · often 1–5 min on 7B CPU — background only, never touches the engine.

No saved analyses yet — every “Root-cause dive” (even a failed one) will be stored here so you can track how conclusions change over time.
